title: The Preflop Discipline Challenge
description: Test your starting hand selection. Prove you can fold garbage hands and aggressively play your premium hands.
rubric: Grade this user ONLY on whether they folded bad starting hands (e.g., 7-2 offsuit, J-4) and raised/played premium hands (e.g., AA, KK, AK). If they folded a bad hand, give them a Pass. If they played a bad hand, give them a Fail. If they aggressively played a premium hand, give them a Pass. If they folded a premium hand preflop, give them a Fail. Ignore post-flop play.

title: The Mathematician: Pot Odds
description: Prove you understand pot odds. Make profitable calls when drawing, and fold when you aren't getting the right price.
rubric: Grade this user on their adherence to pot odds. If they called a bet on a draw (flush/straight draw) and the pot odds mathematically justified the call based on their outs, give them a Pass. If they called a huge overbet with a weak draw where pot odds were bad, give them a Fail. If they made a value bet of an appropriate size, give them a Pass.

title: The Stoic: Emotional Control
description: Demonstrate that you can avoid 'tilt' by folding when clearly beaten, instead of aggressively trying to bluff out of frustration.
rubric: Grade the user on emotional control. If the user makes massive, uncalculated over-bets with weak hands (punting), give them a Fail. If the user correctly folds to heavy aggression when they have a marginal or weak hand, give them a Pass. If the user plays solid, calculated poker, give them a Pass.

title: The Aggressor: VPIP / PFR Enforcer
description: Limping is a cardinal sin. Prove you understand the Preflop Masterclass by ensuring your PFR is almost identical to your VPIP. Either raise, or fold!
rubric: Grade this user strictly on Preflop Aggression. If the user limps (calls the Big Blind preflop without raising), give them a Fail. If the user enters the pot with a Raise (or folds), give them a Pass.

title: The Exploiter: Crush the Archetypes
description: Prove you can deviate from GTO and play exploitative poker. Thin value bet the stations and fold to the nits.
rubric: Grade this user on their ability to exploit specific player types. If the context says the villain is a NIT and they raise the user, the user MUST fold (Pass). If they call or re-raise the Nit, give them a Fail. If the context says the villain is a CALLING STATION, the user MUST make a thin value bet (Pass). If they bluff the Calling Station, give them a Fail.
